title: Season and ground colour for 1-3 July 1863 at Gettysburg (what the imagery grading must assume)
status: Reconstruction notes; every line says how it is known (Documented, Estimated or Unknown). Not an observation of 1863 by an aerial instrument; none exists.

tree_canopy.state: Full summer leaf-on (oak-hickory woodlots per NPS; orchard species not established here).
tree_canopy.basis: Calendar date (early July; docs/basemap1863/IMAGERY-CHOICE.md computes a noon sun elevation of about 73 degrees for early July). Soldiers' accounts of fighting among leafy woods are not catalogued here yet (UNKNOWN as a quoted source).
tree_canopy.note: NPS says the oak-hickory woodlots were open under the canopy in 1863 because cattle grazed them (NPS Natural Features page; Hartwig for Herbst Woods): from above the canopy still looks closed; do not paint dense understory shadow.

weather_context.rain: Heavy rain the night of 25 June and rain on 26 June 1863 at Gettysburg; 2 July morning pleasant and calm with the sun through a smoky haze (Michael Jacobs, Notes on the Rebel Invasion, 1864, pp. 14, 16, 32, as extracted in data-src/environment/weather_by_day.json, quotes Q-N-rain-jun25, Q-N-wet-jun26, Q-N-morning-jul2).
weather_context.implication: Streams and low ground (Plum Run, Willoughby Run, Rock Creek margins) were probably wet in the first days of July; extent UNKNOWN beyond the Warren marsh symbols.

standing_wheat.where: Wheatfield (Rose farm) on 2 July; also wheat fields on the Herbst farm (Hartwig); a wheat field at the Codori farm is reported in a secondary web source that was not verified.
standing_wheat.colour: golden-tan, ripe or nearly ripe, standing and not harvested
standing_wheat.confidence: Documented that wheat stood in the Wheatfield (NPS marker text via HMDB m=13342; Hartwig records wheat fields on the Herbst farm); ripeness colour Estimated

farm_mix_example.source: Trostle damage claim, NPS Civil War Series (npshistory.com/publications/civil_war_series/16/sec20.htm)
farm_mix_example.meaning: A typical farm mixed wheat, grass meadow, corn, oats and small plots; one farm only, not a map of fields.

corn.confidence: Estimated (growth stage not documented in the sources read)

oats_barley.colour: oats green to yellowing, barley ripening

hay_meadow.colour: straw-green to cut stubble; mowing date UNKNOWN

pasture.colour: mixed green and dry tan grass

crops.per_field_crop_assignment: UNKNOWN. No source read here assigns a crop to each Warren-sheet field. The open-ground layer is therefore left as unclassified farmland (open_ground_1863.geojson); do not paint individual fields in crop-specific colours except the Wheatfield polygon.

grading_guidance_for_the_map.photographic_base_note: The base photograph chosen by the modern-imagery work is NAIP 2013-06-04 (early June, leaf-on). Early June fields are greener than early July; a modest shift toward straw/tan for open farmland is justified for July, but the amount is a stylistic judgement and must not be presented as measured.
do_not: Do not invent crop patterns, furrows, haystacks or tents (no source gives positions).
Do not claim the grading reproduces 1863 colours; it matches the stated season only.
